page.title: Panel declarations and per-step changes
page.description: How Flowview panels change per step today, every variant shown with live panels, and a proposed step-level panelDeclare map.

sections.heading: How panel state changes per step today: the common rules
text: Not every rule here applies to every panel. Most of this tab is the common fold used by 22 of the 42 types; the other 20 types have custom folds with their own rules (Special fold rules tab). The last row of the table at every step says exactly which types the rule covers.
Each panel beside the diagram is a real Flowview panel demonstrating the rule its title names; the table shows exactly what that step wrote. Counts and rates are illustrative.

panels.title: What this step wrote (this table's rows are replaced every step)

steps.text: **The declaration is fixed.** Each panel is declared once: `type`, `title`, fixed fields such as the gauge's `max` and `unit`, and an optional `initial` starting state.
**A patch carries forward.** The gauge patch is shallow-merged into the previous snapshot, so 40 stays until a later step changes it.

cells.value: 22 common-fold types; custom folds carry by their own rules

steps.text: **`log` lines append** instead of replacing. The gauge has no patch, so it keeps 40.
**`enterOnce` lasts one step.** The gauge shows 380 here only; the carried value stays 40 underneath. In a common-fold panel, appended keys such as `log` cannot be set through `enterOnce`.

cells.value: 22 common-fold types; custom folds differ (Special tab)

steps.text: **`null` is stored as a value; each renderer decides what it means.** The gauge renders a missing number as 0. Other types differ: table `rows: []` clears, funnel and grid treat `null` as delete (next steps).

cells.value: storing null: common fold; its meaning: each renderer

steps.text: **Key-by-key merge.** This patch names `clean` and `kept`; the funnel keeps `raw` from the previous step. Funnel `counts`, grid `cells`/`marks` and seatmap `sold`/`held`/`price`/`tierOf` use this rule.
**`enterOnce` in a custom fold follows that fold's rule.** The funnel merges one-step counts over the carried counts: `kept` shows 500 here and returns to 870 next step.

cells.value: funnel and grid one-step entries only

steps.text: **No funnel patch: the carried counts return.** `kept` shows 870 again; the one-step 500 is gone.
**Per-key delete.** In a merge map, `null` for one key forgets that key; `raw` and `clean` stay.

cells.rule: kept forgotten; raw and clean stay

steps.text: **Whole-map clear.** `counts: null` forgets every key at once. (Elsewhere: a table's `rows: []` clears by replacement; a device-app card property such as `{"icon": null}` restores its declared value, while `null` for a whole card clears that card. The property case is on the Special fold rules tab.)
**Story time.** The clock moves 5 hours and nobody patches the battery: its fold drains 4 % per hour (illustrative rate) from elapsed time.

cells.value: battery, phone, deviceapp, appscreens, with storyTime declared

steps.text: **Visibility is a step-level map.** `panelVisibility` hides the funnel. Its content keeps folding while hidden: this step also writes all three counts.

**A few types let a step override a declared value.** The radar declares `threshold: 80`; this step writes 50 and the arc moves. The funnel reappears with the counts written while hidden. Full list: Panel types tab.

cells.value: only the types listed on the Panel types tab

steps.text: **The gap.** For most fields the renderer always receives the same declaration. To show this gauge in watts with a 200 maximum later, an author must declare a second gauge and switch visibility, or the type must add its own override key.

cells.value: all 42 types, for every field without a per-type override

steps.text: **Alternate paths fold independently.** On this path the gauge goes to 5 and the log never receives a line.

sections.heading: Buffer: range paint accumulates
text: Operations that only some panel types accept, one section per case. Each section has its own steps, its one panel and the JSON each step wrote. Times and rates are illustrative.
Buffer `mark` paints add up across steps; `enterOnce.mark` replaces them for one step; `cells` replaces everything.

steps.text: **Range paint accumulates.** Buffer `mark` ranges are added to every earlier paint, like `log` lines.
**A second paint lands on top** of the first: cells 2–5 become uploading, 0–1 stay buffered.
**Exception: `enterOnce.mark` replaces the paint list for one step.** Only cells 6–8 show as dropped here; the next step shows the accumulated paint again.
**Back to the accumulated paint.** No patch: cells 0–5 show the two earlier paints again.
**`cells` replaces everything and clears earlier paint.**

sections.heading: Home map: transient signals
text: Home-map `signals` draw at their step only; device states carry.

steps.text: **A purely transient patch.** Home-map `signals` draw a message from the porch camera to the hub at this step only and leave nothing in carried state; the camera's `detect` state does carry.

cells.rule: signal this step only; detect carried

steps.text: **Next step, no patch:** no signal is drawn; the camera stays in `detect`. Compare the Strand scene section, where a cut's result is carried.

sections.heading: Zoneframe: whole-array state by id
text: A `zones` patch replaces the whole carried array; zones it does not list show their declared state.

steps.text: **Whole-array state by id.** The patch lists only the walkway (masked). The fold carries this array as given; the renderer shows the door at its declared state.

**A second patch replaces the array, it does not merge.** It lists only the door (ignored), so the walkway returns to its declared armed state. Compare the Strand scene section, where each actor carries independently.

sections.heading: Inflight: start, mark, end
text: Operations apply in the order start, end, mark; finished bars stay on the axis.

panels.title: Inflight: start, mark, end; history kept

steps.text: **Inflight operations.** `start` opens a bar in each lane at this step.
**`end` closes a bar; `mark` recolours an open one.** Operations in one patch apply in the order start, end, mark.
**History is kept.** The upload bar closes; both finished bars stay on the axis.

sections.heading: Device app: notifications
text: `notify` adds cards; `clear` removes the stack first.

panels.title: Device app: notifications, report times, card overrides

steps.text: **Notifications accumulate**, newest first.
**`clear` then `notify` in one patch:** the stack is cleared first, then the new card is added.

sections.heading: Device app: report freshness
text: `reportedAt` stamps a card; later steps age it from story time.

panels.title: Device app: notifications, report times, card overrides

steps.text: **A report time.** `reportedAt: "now"` stamps the battery card with this step's story time.
**Freshness and drain come from elapsed time.** Two hours later the card reads "Updated 2 h ago" and the battery has drained 4 % (2 % per hour, illustrative), with no patch to either.

sections.heading: Battery: anchor and one-step drain
text: `charge` sets the value exactly; `drain` subtracts once.

steps.text: **`charge` is an anchor.** The battery shows exactly 90; drift continues from it. A `drain` in the same patch would be ignored.
**`drain` is a one-step operation.** 5 % is subtracted at this step (85 %); it is not repeated at later steps.

sections.heading: Device app: overriding a declared card value
text: A card property overrides its declared value; `null` restores it.

panels.title: Device app: notifications, report times, card overrides

steps.text: **A card field can override a declared value.** The model card's declared icon is `camera`; this step sets `chip`.
**`null` restores the declared value** for that card field.

sections.heading: Strand scene: one-step and carried events
text: Per-actor state carries; `enterOnce.events` lasts one step; ordinary `events` leave a carried result.

panels.title: Strand scene: step-local events, carried results
panels.label: restriction cut

steps.text: **Per-item state keyed by declared ids.** The enzyme moves to position 11 and binds. `actors` sets state for the declared actor; it does not replace the declaration.
**A one-step event.** `enterOnce.events` cuts the strand for this step only; its result is shown here and discarded afterwards.
**Next step: the strand is whole again.** The displayed snapshot at the previous step is not the carried state, which is why a resume point must come from carried state.
**A step-local event with a carried result.** The `cut` event plays at this step only; the cut strand is carried to later steps.
**Next step, no patch:** the strand stays cut. No event replays.

sections.heading: enterOnce support by type
text: What a one-step override does in each kind of panel.

steps.text: **`enterOnce` support is type-specific.** Common fold: any field for one step; `log` cannot be set through it, and buffer `mark` replaces the paint list (Buffer section). Funnel and grid merge one-step entries. Phone accepts only `enterOnce.audio`. Device app has none. Other custom folds define their own rules.

cells.value: any field; log excluded; mark replaces

sections.heading: Where each of the 42 panel types sits today
text: Read from the registered panel definitions on `main` (5744ca77). A step writes panel state under `steps[i].panels.<id>`; the older spelling `steps[i].patch.<id>` is still accepted, and when both are present `panels` is used.

bullets.text: **Common fold** (22 types): shallow merge per key, `log` appends, buffer `mark` paints accumulate (compacted when more than 64 accumulate), `enterOnce` for one step: state, leds, gauge, log, image, waterfall, orbit, zoneframe, xray, queue, thermo, buffer, radar, signal, tiles, table, data-contract, checks, budget, cost, trace, replicas.

**Custom fold** (20 types), each with its own rules: screen, battery, homemap, inflight, phone, deviceapp, appscreens, timeline, sequence, reads, frames, locus, funnel, grid, strandscene, cellscene, seatmap, chime, dispatch, security.
**Key-by-key merge maps** (`null` deletes one key, a whole-field `null` deletes all): funnel `counts`; grid `cells` and `marks`; seatmap `sold`, `held`, `price`, `tierOf`.
**Accumulating fields**: `log` (all common-fold types); buffer `mark`; timeline `events` and `miss` (added to the declared events); phone and deviceapp `notify`, with `clear`.
**Step-local events with carried results**: strandscene and cellscene `events`.
**Purely transient patches** (drawn at their step, nothing carried): homemap `signals`.
**Derived from story time**: battery drain and charge (with `charge` anchors and one-step `drain`); phone, deviceapp and appscreens clock and date; deviceapp card freshness from `reportedAt`.

**A step overrides a declared value** (built into each type): data-contract `columns`, `fields`, `fieldWidth`; screen and security `scene`; radar `threshold`; deviceapp card `source`, `icon`, `badgeMode`, `badgeText`, `badgeColor` (`null` restores the declared value); strandscene actor `label` and cellscene item `label`; seatmap `tierOf` (overrides a section's declared `tier`; deleting the entry restores it); homemap device and subject `icon` (`null` restores the declared icon).

**Whole-value state keyed by declared ids** (common fold: each patch replaces the whole carried value; the renderer fills in ids the value does not list): zoneframe `zones` (unlisted zones show their declared state), xray `layers` (unlisted layers show sealed), replicas `replicas`, an object keyed by replica id (unlisted replicas show unknown).
**Per-item carried state keyed by declared ids** (custom fold; each item carries independently): strandscene `actors`, cellscene `items`.
**Not changeable per step**: every other declaration field, for example gauge `max` and `unit`, funnel `stages`, table `columns`, and every panel's card `title`.

sections.heading: Proposed change: a step-level panelDeclare map
text: A design proposal, not shipped behaviour. One entry shape covers both lasting and timed overrides: `{"set": {…}, "steps": N}`. The tables and checks on this tab are authored to explain the design; they do not run it. It replaces the reserved `declare` key inside panel patches from PR #643 and answers the gpt-6-astra review of that PR. One decision is open: how folding treats earlier steps (step 5).

panels.title: What this step writes or decides
Gauge: effective declaration at this step
What the proposal must guarantee (authored status, not test results)

checks.label: No collision with any panel state key
Fork panel types need no upstream registration
Validation and fold use one merge
Story time, evidence and references follow it
Existing per-type override keys keep working
Older viewers report the missing feature

steps.text: **One entry shape, keyed by panel id**, beside `panelVisibility`, so it never shares a name with a panel's own state keys and works with both `panels` and legacy `patch` spellings: `"panelDeclare": {"gauge": {"set": {"max": 200}, "steps": 3}}`. `set` holds declaration fields; `steps` is how many steps the entry lasts on this path, counting its own step (default: until the path ends). Keeping fields inside `set` means `steps` never collides with a declaration field of the same name.

cells.rule: no steps: lasts to the end of the path (step 2)

steps.text: **Effective declaration** = the authored declaration with every entry active at this step applied in step order (later entries win). An entry is active from its own step for `steps` steps on this path. When it expires, its keys return to what they would be without it. `null` inside `set` restores the declared value while the entry is active. `id`, `type`, `initial`, `visible` are reserved inside `set`. Merge depth: each top-level declaration field is replaced whole, including arrays and objects such as `fields` or `stages`; nothing is merged inside them.

noop.detail: no panelDeclare: the authored declaration object is used unchanged

steps.text: **A timed entry.** This step writes `{"set": {"max": 50}, "steps": 1}`: the gauge uses 50 here. Next step the entry has expired and max is 200 again, from the earlier entry that is still active. `steps: 3` would hold 50 for this step and the next two.

cells.rule: active for 3 steps on this path

noop.detail: no panelDeclare: the authored declaration object is used unchanged

steps.text: **Validated where written**, with warnings at `steps[i].panelDeclare.<id>.<field>`; an override with errors is ignored. The rest of the patch is checked against what the renderer will use: for types with their own override keys (data-contract `fields`), state overrides win over the effective declaration in both validation and rendering.

noop.detail: no panelDeclare: the authored declaration object is used unchanged

agree.detail: one helper builds the effective declaration for both

steps.text: **Folding: a decision is needed.** Option A, segment fold: each declaration change starts a new segment seeded from the carried state (without `enterOnce` overlays or one-step operations such as `drain`), so earlier steps are never reinterpreted; every fold needs a defined resume point, and phone, deviceapp, homemap and inflight need one written first. Option B, whole-path refold (PR #643): simpler, but a later declaration can make an earlier ignored patch take effect (for example a grid key declared later).

cells.rule: no reinterpretation; folds need a resume point
A→B→A is three segments; resume state is part of the key
earlier patches and story-time intervals change

Under Option B the new rate applies to every earlier interval as well.

steps.text: **Viewers and editors.** Specs that use it are stamped `steps.panel-declare`; an older viewer reads the stamp and reports the missing feature, then renders the authored declaration. An unstamped spec in an older viewer ignores the key silently. Backstage and native viewers share the player. The desktop workbench edits it in its own inspector group.

steps.text: **Why not a key inside the panel patch (PR #643).** A Signal link may have id `declare`; on `main` the patch `{"declare": {"state": "ok"}}` updates that link. With a reserved key inside panel patches, the same patch would be read as a declaration override, with no warning.
